sentences.text: Scientists know this genus from two well-preserved three-dimensional braincases.
Alan Pradel, Paul Tafforeau, John G. Maisey, and Philippe Janvier first named Kawichthys in 2011.
The type species of the genus is Kawichthys moodiei, which serves as the species the genus is based on.
Kawichthys belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fish.
The genus is classified within the extinct order Symmoriiformes.
Fossils were found in Upper Pennsylvanian deposits in Kansas, United States.
Specimens were collected from the Douglas Group, located between the Haskell Limestone and the lower beds of the overlying Robbins Shale.
Kawichthys lived during the Gzhelian stage, between 303.7 and 298.9 million years ago.
